# sendmulticast

Sends the data to the multicast host. *(version 4.62 or later)*

```ttl
sendmulticast <multicastname> <data1> <data2>....
```

## Remarks

Causes Tera Term to sends characters to the multicast terminal specified by &lt;multicastname&gt; argument or [command line option](https://teratermproject.github.io/manual/5/en/html/commandline/teraterm.html). Beforehand, the name of terminal identification must be configured by using [setmulticastname](setmulticastname.md) command.
If &lt;data&gt; is a string, the string is sent to the host.
If &lt;data&gt; is an integer, its lowest-order byte (0-255) is regarded as an ASCII code of the character, and the character is sent to the host.

NOTICE: Sent data is ignored on the terminal the [AcceptBroadcast](https://teratermproject.github.io/manual/5/en/html/menu/setup-additional.html) is disabled.

## Example

```ttl
; TerminalA
setmulticastname 'screen1'
; Do not receive any strings.
```

```ttl
; TerminalB
setmulticastname 'screen2'
; The 'violin' string will be sent by the TerminalD.
```

```ttl
; TerminalC
setmulticastname 'screen2'
; The 'violin' string will be sent by the TerminalD.
```

```ttl
; TerminalD
setmulticastname 'screen3'
sendmulticast 'screen2' 'violin' 13 10     ; Multicast transmission
; Do not receive any strings.
```
